Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
HOOK, IUCD, SHIRODKAR'S PATTERN 



( Reaffirmed 1997) 



1. Scope— Dimensional and other requirements for Shirodkar f s pattern IUCD hook used In 

obstetrics. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 HOOK, IUCD, SHIRODKAR'S PATTERN 

2.1 A deviation of ± 25 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material —Stainless steel conforming to Designation 20Cr13 or 30CM3 of IS:6603-1972 
1 Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The hook shall be free from pits, burrs, cracks and other defects. 

4.2 The tip of the hook and all other edges shall be smoothly rounded off. 

4.3 The hook shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment — The instrument shall be hardened and tempered to give hardness of 370 to 
430 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Grip the hook firmly in a vice, close to its joint to the handle, with the handle protruding out. 
Try to rotate the handle by gripping it between the index finger and the thumb of right hand with 
normal force. It shall not be possible to move the handle.

IS: 7725- 1975 

6.2 Grip the shaft firmly in a vice close to angle along its axis so that 80 mm of the shaft above angle 
protrude out and tip faces upward. Suspend weight from the tip gradually increasing to 5 kg and 
allow it to act for 2 minutes. Release the load. No permanent set shall be observed after completion 
of the test 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The instrument shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as 
mentioned in IS: 7531-1975 'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of 
stainless steel surgical instruments '. 

6.4 Subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier the instrument may be put to the 
following test. 

6.4*1 Copper sulphate test — Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at room 
temperature for 6 minutes and wash off with fresh water or wet cotton wool. Composition of the 
solution shall be as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CuS0 4 .5H 2 ) 4'0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H 2 S0 4 ) ( sp gr 184 ) 10'0 g 

Distilled water [ see IS : 1070-1960 Specification for 90'0 ml 
water, distilled quality ( revised) ] 

No red stains or spots on the sample shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface may 
be permitted. 

7. Marking — Each hook shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade- 
mark and the words ' stainless steel '. 

7.1 iSf Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The hook shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bag. 
Each hook shall then be packed in cartons. The packing may also be done as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the supplier.
